saints.name: St. Apollinaris
saints.title: Bishop and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: The first bishop of Ravenna, honored as a martyr from the earliest Christian centuries…
biography: Apollinaris, venerated as the first bishop of Ravenna, is placed by ancient tradition among the disciples of St. Peter, who sent him — probably from Antioch — to preach the Gospel in that imperial Adriatic port. The Roman Martyrology says he 'honoured the Church of Classis near Ravenna by a glorious martyrdom.'

His seventh-century Acts, of doubtful history, relate that during a ministry of some twenty-six years he was repeatedly scourged, driven into exile, and at last beaten near Classis in the days of Vespasian, dying of his wounds while foretelling the Church's final triumph; some modern writers place him rather in the late second century.

His cult at Ravenna is ancient and splendid: the basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe, consecrated in 549, still shows his image in its great mosaic, and in 856 his relics were moved to Sant'Apollinare Nuovo for fear of Saracen raids. He is patron of Ravenna, whose church he founded.

His feast, long kept on 23 July, was dropped from the general calendar in 1969 and restored in 2002 on 20 July, 23 July belonging to St. Bridget of Sweden. He is also numbered among the saints invoked against gout and epilepsy.
saints.knownFor: The apostolic evangelization of Ravenna and his martyrdom.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
